row.정의: 우울증 환자 시뮬레이터가 인간 환자 대화와 얼마나 일치하는지를 해석 가능하고 임상적으로 의미 있게 평가하는 프레임워크. 서사·감정 과정, 감정가, 어휘 다양성, 응답 길이, 우울 언어 표지의 5개 차원을 인간 기준 대화와 비교해 0~100 유사도로 환산한다.
row.대표 과제: 환자 메시지를 Problem, Transition, Change, Filler로 분류해 대화 진행을 비교하는 과제 등 5개 차원 평가
row.대표 예시·설명: 환자 프로필로 시뮬레이터가 만든 대화와 인간 환자 대화를 같은 차원으로 각각 평가한 뒤 통계를 비교하는 과제 설명(실제 문항 아님)
row.이용 시 유의사항: 라이선스, 상업적 이용, 수정·파생, 재배포, lm-eval 지원 여부는 확인하지 않았다. 논문은 코드와 시뮬레이션 대화 데이터셋을 공개한다고 밝히지만 라이선스는 명시하지 않는다. 기준 데이터는 다른 출처인 Eeyore의 영어 대화(크라우드소싱·연기 대화)이므로 해당 약관을 별도로 확인해야 한다. 진짜 임상 기록이 아닌 대리 대화이며, 분류에 LLM(gpt-oss-120b)을 사용한다.

english_copy.axis: Agents and safety (fidelity evaluation of depression patient simulators)
english_copy.definition: A framework for interpretable, clinically meaningful evaluation of how closely depression patient simulators match human patient conversations. It compares simulated and human dialogues on five dimensions (narrative-emotion processes, emotional valence, lexical diversity, response length, linguistic markers of depression), converted to 0-100 similarity scores.
english_copy.task: Classify patient messages as Problem, Transition, Change, or Filler to compare dialogue progression, plus the other four dimensions
english_copy.example: Task description (not an actual test item): a simulator is conditioned on a patient profile to generate a conversation, and both the simulated and human conversations are evaluated on the same dimensions and compared.

screening.paper_title: PSI-Bench: Interpretable and Clinically Meaningful Evaluation of Depression Patient Simulators
screening.abstract: Patient simulators are gaining traction in mental health training by providing scalable exposure to complex and sensitive patient interactions. Simulating depressed patients is challenging, as safety constraints and high patient variability complicate simulations and underscore the need for simulators that capture diverse and realistic patient behaviors. However, existing evaluations heavily rely on LLM-judges with poorly specified prompts and do not assess behavioral diversity. We introduce PSI-Bench, an automatic evaluation framework that provides interpretable, clinically meaningful diagnostics of depression patient simulator behavior across turn-, dialogue-, and population-level dimensions. Using PSI-Bench, we benchmark seven LLMs across two simulator frameworks and find that simulators produce overly long, lexically diverse responses, show reduced variability, and move through therapeutic stages and toward positive valence too quickly. We also show that the simulation framework has a larger impact on fidelity than the model scale. Results from a human study demonstrate that our benchmark is strongly aligned with judgments of mental health professionals. Our work reveals key limitations of current depression patient simulators and provides an interpretable, extensible benchmark to guide future simulator design and evaluation.
